# Results — Study 797 (FX Value / PPP real-rate mean reversion)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test —
**currencies whose real exchange rate is undervalued vs their own long-run average
subsequently appreciate** (the FX value factor). Offline & deterministic once cached;
run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number. As-of **2025-06-30** (the
last complete month with CPI on every G10 leg at publication; the partial current month
is dropped). Fingerprints `fx=0f1dcad0ff54` (FX month-end, USD-per-foreign) and
`cpi=4553d2b68c91` (CPI panel).*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| FX tape | yfinance daily G10 spot vs USD, normalised to USD-per-foreign, sampled to month-end; 9 legs (EUR JPY GBP AUD NZD CAD CHF SEK NOK) |
| CPI tape | IMF IFS monthly `PCPI_IX` (US JP GB CA CH SE NO) + Eurostat HICP `CP00.EA19` (EUR) + IMF IFS **quarterly** `PCPI_IX` for AUD & NZD (they publish CPI only quarterly), forward-filled to month-end within each quarter |
| Real rate | `log q_i = log S_i(USD/FX) + log CPI_i − log CPI_US`; high q = rich (overvalued), low q = cheap (undervalued) |
| Signal | `value_i,t = trailing-mean(log q_i, 60m, min 36m) − log q_i,t` (positive = cheap); cross-sectional dollar-neutral rank weights, long cheap / short rich |
| Execution lag | one shift: signal formed at close of month *t* (FX(t), CPI known through *t−1* — a **1-month publication lag** baked in) earns month *t+1* spot return |
| Costs | one-way × NAV turnover both legs; **shorts pay a 100 bps/yr borrow/financing spread** on gross short notional |

**Survivorship (Signal axis):** the G10 basket is a fixed, current-membership set of
major currencies; none of the nine were dropped or redenominated over the sample, so
there is no survivor-selection tilt — but it *is* a developed-market, ex-post "these are
the majors" basket, and the FX-value premium is documented to live disproportionately in
**emerging** currencies this study deliberately excludes.

## The headline — value long-short (long cheap / short rich), monthly

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| months | 246 (2005-01 → 2025-06) |
| mean monthly return | +8.52 bps |
| annualized return | **+1.02%** |
| annualized vol | 3.39% |
| annualized Sharpe | **0.30** |
| one-sample *t* | +1.37 |
| **Newey-West (6-lag) *t*** | **+1.58** |
| hit rate (months positive) | 129/246 = **52.4%** (Wilson 95% [46.2%, 58.6%]) |

The value tilt is **directionally right** — cheap currencies do outrun rich ones, +1.0%/yr
gross — but the effect **does not clear the desk's `t ≥ 2` bar** on this G10 tape. The
autocorrelation-robust *t* is +1.58; the one-sample *t* is +1.37.

## Placebo — random cross-sectional sign flips

Independently flipping each month's cross-sectional weight signs at random (gross book
and return tape held fixed), 20 seeds × 500 draws = 10,000 random books:

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| observed Sharpe | 0.302 |
| placebo mean Sharpe | −0.001 (sd 0.223) |
| right-tail **p** | **0.0905** |

About **1 random book in 11** beats the real value sort — consistent with a modest,
uncertified positive tilt, not a fluke of sign, but not significant at 5% either.

## Robustness — trailing-window sweep

| trailing window | Sharpe | NW *t* |
|---|--:|--:|
| 36 months | 0.20 | +0.92 |
| 48 months | 0.25 | +1.29 |
| **60 months** (headline) | **0.30** | **+1.58** |
| 84 months | 0.30 | +1.64 |

Longer memory helps a little and the sign is stable, but no window certifies the effect.

## Sub-period (a snooped split, reported honestly)

| era | months | Sharpe | NW *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 2005 → 2014 | 120 | 0.06 | +0.24 |
| 2015 → 2025-06 | 126 | 0.66 | **+2.15** |

The premium is **entirely a post-2015 phenomenon** on this tape — flat in the first
decade, *t* = +2.15 in the second. This split is **not pre-registered**, so it is a
hypothesis for follow-up (does G10 value only pay when rate-vol is high / the dollar
cycle turns?), **not** a certification: the full-sample number governs the stamp.

## The timer — costs and borrow

Turnover ≈ 0.30 (one-way) per month; shorts pay 100 bps/yr borrow:

| one-way cost | gross ann | net ann | net Sharpe | net NW *t* | worst month |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 5 bps | +1.02% | **+0.34%** | 0.10 | +0.53 | −3.73% |
| 10 bps | +1.02% | +0.16% | 0.05 | +0.25 | −3.73% |
| 20 bps | +1.02% | **−0.20%** | −0.06 | −0.32 | −3.73% |

The ~1%/yr gross edge is **too thin to survive its own frictions**: borrow on the short
book plus rebalancing cost eats most of it at a retail 5 bps, and the net return goes
**negative by a realistic institutional 20 bps**. Tradability is a `MIRAGE`.

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased

Deterministic panel of log real rates with a TUNABLE planted mean reversion; no network.

| world | NW *t* of the value sort |
|---|--:|
| null (value_strength = 0), 20 seeds | mean **+0.34** (sd 0.87), \|t\| ≥ 2 in **1/20** (≈ nominal 5%) |
| planted reversion (value_strength = 0.15), seed 797 | **+12.44** (Sharpe 2.24, +7.3%/yr) |

The detector sits at ~0 on the null (firing at the nominal false-positive rate) and
lights up hard on a planted PPP pull. The harness *can* bank the effect it is designed
to harvest — so the sub-2 real-tape *t* is a property of the **G10 tape**, not a broken
pipeline. *(A machinery/power check only — never cited for the real-tape stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — WEAK.** Long-cheap/short-rich G10 currencies earns **+1.02%/yr**, Sharpe
  **0.30**, but the autocorrelation-robust **NW *t* = +1.58** (one-sample +1.37, placebo
  *p* = 0.09) — below the desk's `t ≥ 2` bar. The value tilt is real in *direction* and
  matches a large literature, but **this G10-only tape cannot certify it**. (The
  premium is documented to be stronger in emerging currencies, which this study
  excludes.) Literature says real; this tape reads `WEAK`.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** Net Sharpe 0.10 at a retail 5 bps and **negative by 20 bps**
  once turnover and short borrow are charged — the ~1%/yr gross cushion is thinner than
  its own frictions.
